claims.text: The target material is a Ta-based refractory BCC high-entropy alloy such as MoNbTiTa.
Standard experimental melting data are unavailable for the target alloy.
Full ab initio free-energy calculations are computationally prohibitive for the target alloy.
A Ta-alloy MTP can be trained using constrained-DFT configurations containing lattice compression and extension, random displacements, relaxations, and magnetic-moment perturbations.
Actively learned MTPs have been used to evaluate surface and unstable stacking-fault energies in MoNbTi and MoNbTiTa refractory alloys.
Sampling unstable stacking faults and surface configurations explicitly covers the high-entropy liquid structure.
An MTP can replace full phase-space thermodynamic integration with a reduced perturbation or harmonic-reference scheme near and above the solidus.
Magnetic MTPs trained by constrained DFT can treat magnetic moments alongside atomic positions and lattice vectors in multicomponent Fe-Al alloys.
The cited Fe-Al MTP reproduces formation-energy trends and lattice parameters accurately.
Surface and unstable stacking-fault energies are critical determinants of nucleation and melting in refractory alloys.
MTPs capture complex local chemical environments and applicable magnetic contributions that empirical potentials miss.
Existing EAM potentials fail to capture complex liquid structure in multicomponent systems.
Active learning on surface and stacking-fault configurations makes the MTP robust in the high-entropy liquid regime.
The resulting perturbation scheme permits accurate free-energy estimation without full thermodynamic integration.
The proposed method will predict the Ta-alloy melting temperature within 5% of a high-fidelity benchmark.
The proposed method will reduce free-energy computation time by more than a factor of 100 relative to full ab initio thermodynamic integration.
The approach may fail in systems with strong directional bonding.
The approach may fail when liquid structure is governed by short-range ordering absent from the training set.
An MTP developed from Fe-Al evidence may not generalize to Ta-based refractory alloys because their electronic structures and bonding differ.
The net cost benefit is uncertain because the cost of producing the active-learning dataset has not been quantified.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis says the training set explicitly covers the high-entropy liquid structure through surface and stacking-fault sampling, while the uncertainty field acknowledges that explicit Ta-liquid configurations may be absent. Surface and defect configurations are not themselves explicit liquid configurations.
